title: "The truth value of an array with more than one element is ambiguous" loading np.array values
body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
def test_construct_from_nparray_value() -> None:
    array_cell = np.array([2, 3])
    df = pl.DataFrame(np.array([[array_cell, 4]], dtype=object))
    assert df.dtypes == [pl.Object, pl.Object]
    to_numpy = df.to_numpy()
    assert to_numpy.shape == (1, 2)
    assert_array_equal(to_numpy[0][0], array_cell)
    assert to_numpy[0][1] == 4
```

### Issue description

The error occurs when creating a DataFrame where a cell is a numpy array (eg pl.List dtype).
This is required for instance if you create a DataFrame were you split a column with `pl.col("name").str.split(", ")`, and you export the data with to_numpy, operate on it and create a new DatFrame with from_numpy`.
This worked on 0.20.5, but was broken by commit c732f26bbd0e60ac72f599a20b4d636913d0f00a where the `v == v ` fails for np.arrays
```
            first_non_nan = next((v for v in values if v == v), None)
```

### Expected behavior

A DataFrame with an object columns is created. See asserts in "reproducible example"
